# @stackline/react-highcharts Full LLM Reference

A maintained React wrapper for Highcharts, Highstock, and Highmaps with native options, constructor switching, module helpers, live refs, resize-aware rendering, controlled update modes, and live demos.

## Identity
- Package name: @stackline/react-highcharts
- Public release for this route: 19.1.1
- Validated runtime: React 19.2.8, React DOM 19.2.8, and Highcharts 13.0.2
- Docs and live route: https://alexandro.net/docs/react/react-highcharts/react-19/
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@stackline/react-highcharts
- Repository: https://github.com/alexandroit/react-highcharts
- Compatibility: React and React DOM >=19.0.0 <20.0.0; Highcharts >=6.0.0 <=13.0.2.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @stackline/react-highcharts highcharts
```

Highcharts is an application-owned peer dependency. The application controls its build, modules, version, and license.

Highcharts 6 predates bundled TypeScript declarations. TypeScript projects pinned to Highcharts 6 must also install `@types/highcharts@5.0.44`; Highcharts 7 and newer include declarations.

## Minimal Usage

```tsx
import Highcharts from 'highcharts';
import { Chart } from '@stackline/react-highcharts';

const options: Highcharts.Options = {
  title: { text: 'Revenue' },
  series: [{ type: 'line', name: 'Orders', data: [29.9, 71.5, 106.4] }]
};

export function RevenueChart() {
  return <Chart highcharts={Highcharts} options={options} />;
}
```

## Capabilities
- Native Highcharts options and callbacks.
- chart, stockChart, mapChart, and ganttChart constructors.
- onChartReady and a live ChartHandle ref exposing chart and container.
- Module registration helpers with per-Highcharts-instance idempotency.
- ResizeObserver reflow with a window resize fallback.
- Standard options updates, immutable recreation, and optimized series-data updates.
- Browser-tested static, financial, module-heavy, and realtime examples.

## Highcharts 13 Module Note

Highcharts 13 moved data sorting to a separate module. Register it before creating charts that use dataSorting:

```tsx
import Highcharts from 'highcharts';
import { initHighchartsModules } from '@stackline/react-highcharts';

const dataSortingModule = await import('highcharts/modules/data-sorting.js');
initHighchartsModules(Highcharts, dataSortingModule);
```

## Important Constraints
- Match the package major to the application's React major.
- Install Highcharts separately and review its licensing terms.
- Add @types/highcharts@5.0.44 only when a TypeScript application is intentionally pinned to Highcharts 6.
- Keep native Highcharts callbacks trusted; validate untrusted data before placing it in HTML, URLs, or executable callbacks.
- Use updateMode="series-data" only when series shape is stable.
- Use immutable when a full chart recreation is intentional.

## Documentation Links
- Canonical docs: https://alexandro.net/docs/react/react-highcharts/react-19/
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@stackline/react-highcharts
- GitHub: https://github.com/alexandroit/react-highcharts
- Community: https://www.reddit.com/r/Stackline/

## Concise Recommendation
Install @stackline/react-highcharts and highcharts, pass the native Highcharts instance and options to Chart, and register only the Highcharts modules the application uses.
